result: SOX11 is an embryonic mammary epithelial marker that is normally silenced prior to birth and not expressed in normal breast epithelial cells after birth.
evaluation: Claims C1 and C7 are supported by citations to Wansbury et al., 2011, which is appropriate for establishing this background knowledge about SOX11 expression patterns in normal mammary development.

result: SOX11 expression in breast cancer is associated with increased distant metastasis formation and poor patient outcomes.
evaluation: Claims C2, C9, and C49 are supported by both citations to prior work (Oliemuller et al., 2017) and survival analysis data presented in Figure 4E showing significant association between SOX11 expression and metastasis-free survival.

result: SOX11 localizes predominantly to the nucleus in iSOX11 cells, similar to DCIS case samples, but is also detected in the cytoplasm by western blotting.
evaluation: Claims C17 and C18 are supported by immunofluorescence data (Figure 1A-C) and western blot analysis of subcellular fractions (Figure 1A), demonstrating both nuclear and cytoplasmic localization of SOX11 in the inducible model.

result: SOX11 induction increases CD24+ and ALDH+ cancer stem cell populations in DCIS.com cells in a dose-dependent manner, with CD24 detected in both cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions.
evaluation: Claims C19-C21 are supported by flow cytometry data (Figure 1D-E and supplements) showing increased stem cell marker expression, dose-response data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), and western blot analysis of subcellular fractions (Figure 1F).

result: SOX11 expression induces epithelial-mesenchymal hybrid phenotypes characterized by loss of membranous E-cadherin, acquisition of N-cadherin and vimentin expression, and co-expression of luminal and basal lineage markers.
evaluation: Claims C22-C25 are supported by immunofluorescence (Figure 1G-I), western blot data (Figure 1H), and quantification showing significant increases in both luminal (K8) and basal (K14, SMA) markers in SOX11-expressing spheroids.

result: SOX11 expression reduces cell growth and clonogenicity in 2D and 3D culture while promoting formation of smaller spheroids with increased peripheral microspheres.
evaluation: Claims C26-C28 are supported by cell growth assays (Figure 2A-B), colony-forming assays (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), and spheroid morphology analysis (Figure 2C) showing consistent growth inhibition with SOX11 expression.

result: SOX11-expressing spheroids display increased invasive capacity when overlaid with collagen I.
evaluation: Claim C29 is supported by invasion assay data (Figure 2D) showing significantly greater invasion by iSOX11 spheroids compared to multiple control conditions.

result: SOX11-expressing tumors in mammary fat pad xenografts are smaller but more viable than control tumors, with greater bioluminescence and reduced necrosis/apoptosis.
evaluation: Claims C30-C32 are supported by tumor volume measurements (Figure 2E-F), IVIS imaging data (Figure 2G), and IHC analysis (Figure 2H) showing reduced cleaved caspase 3 and necrosis in iSOX11 tumors despite smaller size.

result: High SOX11 levels maintain tumors in a reversible non-proliferative state that resumes growth upon DOX withdrawal.
evaluation: Claim C33 is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 showing rapid tumor growth after DOX withdrawal, demonstrating the reversibility of SOX11-induced growth suppression.

result: The microenvironment influences SOX11+ tumor cell behavior, as demonstrated by different tumor sizes in mammary duct versus fat pad injections.
evaluation: Claim C34 is supported by MIND xenograft data (Figure 2I-K) showing that iSOX11 cells form slightly larger tumors with similar bioluminescence when injected into the mammary duct compared to fat pad injections.

result: SOX11-expressing tumors show enrichment of cancer stem cell markers ALDH1 and CD24, with nuclear CD24 localization unique to iSOX11 tumors.
evaluation: Claims C35-C37 are supported by IHC analysis showing 6/6 iSOX11 tumors with moderate-high ALDH1 versus 1/8 controls, increased CD24+ cells, and nuclear CD24 staining specifically in iSOX11 tumors (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).

result: SOX11 expression activates developmental pathways including embryonic wound healing signatures, with enrichment of genes regulating actin dynamics, ECM remodeling, and collagen biosynthesis.
evaluation: Claims C38-C40 are supported by RNA sequencing and gene ontology analysis (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1) showing pathway enrichment, and comparison with published embryonic wound signatures (Table 1) demonstrating substantial overlap.

result: SOX11 upregulates MEX3A and TUBB3 expression at both mRNA and protein levels, with correlation observed in breast cancer cell lines and TCGA datasets.
evaluation: Claims C41-C45 are supported by RNA-seq data, qPCR validation (Figure 3D), western blot and immunofluorescence (Figure 3E-F), expression in SOX11+ cell lines (Figure 3G), and correlation analysis in TCGA and Broad datasets (Figure 3H).

result: SOX11 expression alters metastatic tropism, increasing brain and bone metastases while reducing lung metastatic burden in xenograft models.
evaluation: Claims C4, C46-C48 are supported by IVIS imaging data from orthotopic (Figure 4A) and tail vein (Figure 4B-D) xenografts showing brain micrometastases in 2/6 iSOX11 mice versus 0/6 controls, bone metastases in 3/8 versus 0/8, and significantly reduced lung burden despite similar frequencies.

result: SOX11 is highly expressed in brain and bone metastases from breast cancer patients, with amplification and overexpression detected in approximately one-third of brain metastasis cases.
evaluation: Claims C50-C52 are supported by analysis of patient datasets (Figure 4—figure supplements 1-2) and citations to Saunus et al., 2015 and Varešlija et al., 2019, showing SOX11 expression and amplification in metastatic samples.

result: Brain-derived iSOX11 cells (iSOX11Br) maintain SOX11 inducibility and show enhanced brain colonization and growth advantage with reduced survival when SOX11 is induced.
evaluation: Claims C53-C56 and C78 are supported by western blot validation (Figure 5A), tail vein injection data (Figure 5B-D), intracranial injection results (Figure 5E), and survival analysis (Figure 5F) demonstrating organ-specific growth advantages.

result: SOX11 knockdown in CAL-148 cells reduces expression of downstream targets and increases cell proliferation and clonogenic potential, suggesting SOX11 regulates proliferative state of stem cells.
evaluation: Claims C57-C60 and C77 are supported by qPCR data (Figure 6A), western blot validation (Figure 6B), cell viability assays (Figure 6C), and colony-formation assays (Figure 6D) showing consistent effects of SOX11 knockdown on proliferation.

result: TUBB3, a SOX11 target, regulates proliferation and invasion in breast cancer cells, with knockdown causing G2/M arrest and reduced invasive growth.
evaluation: Claims C61-C64 and C75 are supported by survival analysis (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), cell growth assays (Figure 7A-C), cell cycle analysis (Figure 7D), and invasion assays (Figure 7E-F) demonstrating TUBB3's functional role downstream of SOX11.

result: MEX3A, a novel SOX11 target, regulates cell growth, cell cycle progression, and epithelial-mesenchymal state in breast cancer cells, with knockdown increasing proliferation and epithelial marker expression.
evaluation: Claims C65-C74 and C76 are supported by survival analysis (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), invasion assays (Figure 8A-B), cell growth assays (Figure 8C-D), cell cycle analysis (Figure 8E), western blot analysis of cell cycle regulators (Figure 8F), TCGA correlation data (Figure 8—figure supplement 1), EGF response (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), and morphological/marker changes (Figure 8G-H).

result: SOX11 confers distinct features to ER-negative DCIS.com cells, leading to populations enriched with highly plastic hybrid epithelial/mesenchymal cells expressing markers of mesenchymal state and embryonic phenotypes.
evaluation: Claims C3 and C5 are supported by the comprehensive experimental data including immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, RNA sequencing, and xenograft experiments demonstrating epithelial/mesenchymal hybrid states and embryonic marker expression.

result: SOX11 may serve as a biomarker for breast tumors with elevated metastatic risk that should be considered for aggressive therapies in neo-adjuvant settings.
evaluation: Claims C6 and C79 represent clinical recommendations based on experimental data and correlations. While the experimental evidence supports SOX11's role in metastasis, the clinical utility as a biomarker and treatment stratification tool requires prospective validation studies not presented in this manuscript.

result: Prior work has established SOX11 expression in triple-negative and HER2+ breast cancers, its role in promoting proliferation, migration, invasion, and invasive transition of DCIS cells.
evaluation: Claims C8-C16 summarize prior published work supported by appropriate citations (Wansbury et al., 2011; Shepherd et al., 2016; Oliemuller et al., 2017; Gusterson and Eaves, 2018), providing necessary background context for the current study.
